items.problem: CS0579 'Duplicate ...Attribute' build failure caused by a legacy AssemblyInfo.cs (here Tasks/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs) copied into the tree and compiled alongside the SDK's auto-generated assembly attributes.
items.evidence: lessons.json errors_encountered[2] / skill-defects.json item 1; session-log 6300-6331 (6x CS0579), agent workaround at 6445-6451.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 copied every .cs (excluding only bin/obj); SDK-style WinUI projects default GenerateAssemblyInfo=true, so classic Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs collides with the generated attributes.
items.change: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 now skips *AssemblyInfo.cs on the source copy (preventing CS0579 non-ignorably) and preserves a reference copy under .uwp-source/ so custom attributes (e.g. InternalsVisibleTo) remain recoverable. Documented CS0579 + this behavior in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Common build errors'.
items.expected_effect: The copied tree no longer contains legacy AssemblyInfo.cs, so the first build does not emit CS0579; agents no longer spend a build cycle diagnosing/excluding it.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run of any UWP sample that ships Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs, `dotnet build` produces zero CS0579 errors and no AssemblyInfo.cs appears in the live project tree (only under .uwp-source/).

items.problem: WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC1509/WMC9999 XAML-compiler errors on project-local x:Bind/x:DataType types that are actually a cascade from a C# compile failure; the agent risks rewriting already-correct XAML.
items.evidence: skill-defects.json item 2; session-log 5851-5896 (CS0246 + WMC on MainPage.xaml), MainPage.xaml never re-edited before the green build at 6807.
items.root_cause: A failed C# compile denies MarkupCompilePass2 a LocalAssembly (WMC1509), so every app-defined x:Bind DataType fails to resolve.
items.change: Added a 'Common build errors' subsection: WMC DataType-resolution errors referencing project-local types are usually downstream of CS#### errors — fix the C# first and rebuild before touching XAML; WMC1509 is the tell.
items.expected_effect: Agents stop chasing phantom XAML errors and prioritize the C# fix, reducing failed-build cycles on any migration with app-local compiled bindings.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run where a C# error coexists with WMC0909/WMC1111 on correct XAML, the agent fixes only the C# and the WMC errors clear on rebuild with no XAML edit.

items.problem: CS0246 'DispatcherQueue could not be found' when converting CoreDispatcher.RunAsync in a non-Page helper class.
items.evidence: skill-coverage-gaps.json item 1; session-log 5851-5852 (2x CS0246 in DeviceWatcherHelper.cs); fix injected a DispatcherQueue via ctor + added using.
items.root_cause: The threading pattern's sample shows bare DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue as if ambient and omits `using Microsoft.UI.Dispatching;`; DispatcherQueue is an inherited member only on DependencyObject/Page, not on plain helper classes.
items.change: Sharpened MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#threading: added `using Microsoft.UI.Dispatching;` to the sample and a helper-class rule (inject the Page's this.DispatcherQueue via constructor, or use DispatcherQueue.GetForCurrentThread()).
items.expected_effect: Threading conversions inside non-Page helper classes compile on the first try (correct using + queue acquisition).
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run of a scenario with a non-Page dispatcher helper, DeviceWatcherHelper-style files build with 0 CS0246 for DispatcherQueue.
